h1: Residency Block Schedules, Built For You
paragraph: As a managed service, Scheduling Wizard handles your custom rules to deliver fair, schedules built to the ACGME requirements.

cta.title: Get Your Block Schedule Done Right
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Residency block schedule software automates the creation of year-long rotation assignments for residents across clinical sites, PGY levels, and ACGME-required rotations. Scheduling Wizard takes this a step further as a managed service, instead of operating software yourself, you submit your program's rules and receive the finished schedule, built to the ACGME requirements, delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. No platform to learn, no configuration required.
faq.question: What is residency block schedule software and how does it work?

faq.answer: ACGME compliance is built into the schedule as it is created, not verified manually after the fact. The subspecialty requirements you tell us apply are built in, including duty hour limits, required rotation minimums, and rest requirements. This means the rules are applied while the schedule is built, not discovered after the schedule has already been distributed to residents.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard ensure ACGME compliance in block schedules?

faq.answer: Block scheduling requires balancing dozens of simultaneous rules (PGY requirements, ACGME rules, resident preferences, coverage minimums, and site availability) in a way that is fair and compliant. Most chief residents inherit a blank spreadsheet and very little institutional context, spending dozens of hours on a problem they've never solved before. Scheduling Wizard takes this off the chief by carrying the program's rules forward each year.
faq.question: Why do chief residents struggle with building block schedules each year?

faq.answer: Yes. Scheduling Wizard handles block schedule building, while many of the same programs use their existing platform for day-to-day schedule access. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you that your program can upload directly to whichever viewing platform you already use. Scheduling Wizard and your existing publishing platform are complementary, not mutually exclusive.
faq.question: Can Scheduling Wizard work alongside your existing platform?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard produces Block/Rotation schedules, Call schedules, Clinic schedules, and Attending schedules. All schedule types are built together, so a change in one schedule type automatically resolves dependencies in the others. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you ready for immediate use.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard produce for residency programs?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard serves chief residents, program directors, program coordinators, and GME offices. Chief residents benefit most directly from not having to build or maintain block scheduling software. Program directors benefit from the ACGME rules built in, and institutional continuity across annual chief rotations. Coordinators benefit from expert support on revision handling and rule changes mid-year.

searchIntents: As a residency program director, I'm looking for a software solution that can create ACGME-compliant block schedules efficiently, since managing schedules manually has been too time-consuming and prone to errors.

As a chief resident, I need a tool that helps generate fair and optimized call schedules for my team, without having to learn complex software, because I want to focus on my training rather than administrative tasks.

I'm a program coordinator overwhelmed by the complexities of scheduling for multiple departments; I need a managed service that can handle custom rules, so we can ensure fairness and compliance without needing extensive scheduling knowledge.
As a department chair, I want a solution that keeps institutional continuity across chief resident rotations since this will help maintain our program's stability and compliance with ACGME standards.
